one_sentence: This document establishes a registry of structural isomorphism records documenting cross-domain mappings between physics, theology, and other fields within the Theophysics framework.
executive_summary: This README file serves as the master index for the Isomorphism Registry within the Theophysics Research Initiative. It defines the purpose of each ISO record—to document a claimed structural correspondence between two domains—and outlines the mandatory Four-Test Protocol (HYP-ISO-001) for evaluating all mappings: Prediction Constraint, Symmetric Breaking, Connection Density, and Falsifiability Invitation. The registry currently lists 36 records, ranging from high-confidence structural isomorphisms (e.g., ISO-001 Math/Physics ↔ Trinity) to low-confidence analogies (e.g., ISO-024 8 BCs Uniqueness ↔ Christian Exclusivity). The document concludes with instructions for adding new records, emphasizing honest classification and the requirement that every isomorphism must be falsifiable.
short_summary: This document is the README for the Isomorphism Registry, the central index of cross-domain structural mappings in the Theophysics framework. Its core structural claim is that each ISO record must document a mapping, swap test, bidirectional predictions, falsification criteria, and honest classification. Key evidence includes the Four-Test Protocol and a table of 36 records with varying confidence levels. This matters because it establishes the rigorous methodology and organizational backbone for all isomorphism research within the initiative.
